themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say the model's own week-to-week drift is bigger than any change a brand makes, on cross-channel incrementality they say platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and on identity resolution, B2B buying-group signal loss, and generative content review each model calls out missing or biased ground truth.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, a message, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, trained model, or private chat that now holds it. You can estimate whether the rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removal from a trained model, on B2B buying-group signal loss they say early buying talk now happens in private channels nobody can observe, and on incrementality they note platforms conceal how delivery changes.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models open with a proxy or gateway in front of every write, with spend and audience caps, because sends and spends cannot be rolled back, and the same move appears as a single egress checkpoint for consent and a shared pre-send eligibility check for journey orchestration.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models agree agents profit by passing as human and propose perks or faster endpoints to buy honest disclosure, on journey orchestration they say channel owners paid on their own conversions will subvert a central arbiter, and on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content review all three models build a registry of already-approved claims and admit that deciding whether wording makes a claim, and whether evidence supports it, is a contextual judgment that expert reviewers themselves dispute, and the semantic context layer answers make the same point about the word customer.
